flows.title: Guest decision: Expedia family on a Suite
flows.story: A family of four booked a Suite through Expedia 6+ weeks out and uses an iPhone. Should we send the pre-arrival upsell / app offer?

stages.name: 1 · Guest profile
stages.reading: Held-out reservation #15755, the most typical guest matching the scenario (nearest to the median in feature space).

stages.name: 2 · Selection-bias check
stages.reading: Guests like this are contacted less often than average, so comparing contacted vs un-contacted guests like this one is confounded; the CATE models below adjust for it.

stages.name: 3 · CATE from every model
stages.reading: Every estimator gives its own τ̂ for this guest; the dashed line is the synthetic truth. Causal Forest adds a 95% interval [34.6, 47.7] $ which covers the truth.

stages.name: 4 · Decision
stages.reading: Net value = 0.45 × τ̂ ancillary + $55 × τ̂ direct − $1.50 offer cost.

stages.name: 5 · Counterfactual check (synthetic truth)
stages.reading: Because the DGP is known we can score the decision against the real counterfactual, something a real campaign can only approximate with a holdout.

stages.name: 6 · Cohort context
stages.reading: How this guest compares with others booked through the same channel.

flows.title: Cohort read-out: OTA bookings (Expedia + Booking.com)
flows.story: Does the campaign work for the commission-heavy OTA book of business? Remove selection bias and read the lift for this cohort.

stages.name: 1 · Cohort
stages.reading: Cohort definition and its true (synthetic) effects.

stages.name: 2 · Selection bias
stages.reading: Treated guests in this cohort differ systematically from untreated ones, so the raw difference is not the causal effect.

stages.name: 3a · Adjusted estimate: ancillary
stages.reading: Weighting / doubly-robust estimators pull the naive number back towards the truth (dashed).

stages.name: 3b · Adjusted estimate: direct
stages.reading: Weighting / doubly-robust estimators pull the naive number back towards the truth (dashed).

stages.name: 4 · Covariate balance in cohort
stages.reading: Weights should push every standardised mean difference under 0.10.

stages.name: 5 · CATE models for the cohort (held-out)
stages.reading: Individual-level models agree with the cohort-level estimate: the cohort average of τ̂ is close to the truth.

flows.title: Validity checks: ancillary-spend ATE
flows.story: Before trusting the $ lift: overlap, trimming sensitivity, balance and refutation tests.

stages.name: 1 · Overlap & trimming sensitivity
stages.reading: The estimate should be stable when extreme-propensity guests are trimmed; a drift signals poor overlap.

stages.name: 2 · Covariate balance
stages.reading: Balance is a property of the propensity model, so it is the same for both outcomes.

stages.name: 3 · Built-in refuters (AIPW)
stages.reading: Random cause and subset should leave the effect unchanged; a placebo treatment should give ≈ 0.

stages.name: 4 · DoWhy cross-check
stages.reading: Independent implementation of the same refuters (DoWhy backdoor linear regression).

stages.name: 5 · Verdict
stages.reading: Refuters probe only the observed-confounder model; they cannot rule out unmeasured confounding (none exists here by construction).

flows.title: Campaign policy: baseline, contact the top 30%
flows.story: Marketing can contact 30% of arrivals at $1.50 each. Score everyone, pick the best 30%, compare with random and oracle.

stages.name: 1 · Scoring
stages.reading: Best learner per outcome (by Qini on held-out stays) scores every eligible guest.

chart.title: Ancillary: IPW uplift by score decile ($/guest)

stages.name: 2 · Economics & budget
stages.reading: Net value per guest = margin × τ̂ ancillary + booking value × τ̂ direct − offer cost; contact the top guests with positive value.

stages.name: 3 · Selection
stages.reading: Who gets the offer.

stages.name: 4 · Policy comparison (true $)
stages.reading: Targeting is judged against random picks of the same size and the unattainable oracle. Contacting everyone can win when most guests have positive value.

stages.name: 5 · ROI & risk
stages.reading: Estimated vs true value shows whether the model is over-promising; negative-value contacts are the sleeping-dog leakage.
